## The Machine Learning Workflow

```{=html}
<div class="ml-workflow">

  <div class="ml-step" style="--fill:#E3EDF5; --accent:#557B9E;">
    <span class="ml-step-number">1</span>
    <span class="ml-step-title">Define the objective</span>
    <span class="ml-step-description">What are we trying to learn or predict?</span>
  </div>

  <div class="ml-step" style="--fill:#E3EDF5; --accent:#557B9E;">
    <span class="ml-step-number">2</span>
    <span class="ml-step-title">Understand and prepare the data</span>
    <span class="ml-step-description">What are the characteristics of our data?</span>
  </div>

  <div class="ml-step" style="--fill:#E3F0E8; --accent:#478B77;">
    <span class="ml-step-number">3</span>
    <span class="ml-step-title">Identify candidate models</span>
    <span class="ml-step-description">Which methods are appropriate?</span>
  </div>

  <div class="ml-step" style="--fill:#F8EFD9; --accent:#B28A45;">
    <span class="ml-step-number">4</span>
    <span class="ml-step-title">Train and tune the models</span>
    <span class="ml-step-description">How do we estimate parameters and tune hyperparameters?</span>
  </div>

  <div class="ml-step" style="--fill:#EEE5F4; --accent:#9876AC;">
    <span class="ml-step-number">5</span>
    <span class="ml-step-title">Compare and select a model</span>
    <span class="ml-step-description">Which model best meets our objectives?</span>
  </div>

  <div class="ml-step" style="--fill:#F5E4DD; --accent:#B8735D;">
    <span class="ml-step-number">6</span>
    <span class="ml-step-title">Evaluate the final model</span>
    <span class="ml-step-description">How well does our selected model generalize?</span>
  </div>

  <div class="ml-feedback">
    <span class="ml-feedback-label">Revisit candidate models</span>
  </div>

</div>
```

## Identify Candidate Models: Regression

```{=html}
<div class="rv" style="--a:#478B77;--f:#E3F0E8">

  <div class="rv-nav">
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#557B9E;--f:#E3EDF5">1. Objective</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#557B9E;--f:#E3EDF5">2. Data</div>
    <div class="rv-tab on" style="--a:#478B77;--f:#E3F0E8">3. Candidate models</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#B28A45;--f:#F8EFD9">4. Training &amp; tuning</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#9876AC;--f:#EEE5F4">5. Selection</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#B8735D;--f:#F5E4DD">6. Evaluation</div>
  </div>

  <div class="rv-grid" style="--cols:3">

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>OLS</strong>
      <div>
        <b>Consider:</b> Approximately linear relationship;
        relatively few predictors<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Simple, interpretable<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Sensitive to multicollinearity;
        no unique coefficient estimates when p &gt; n;
        limited flexibility<br>
        <b>Tune:</b> None
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>Ridge</strong>
      <div>
        <b>Consider:</b> Approximately linear relationship;
        many and/or highly correlated predictors<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Stabilizes coefficient estimates;
        accommodates p &gt; n<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Introduces shrinkage bias;
        does not perform feature selection<br>
        <b>Tune:</b> λ (penalty strength)
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>LASSO</strong>
      <div>
        <b>Consider:</b> Approximately linear relationship;
        suspected sparsity or interest in feature selection<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Performs feature selection;
        accommodates p &gt; n<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Introduces shrinkage bias;
        potentially unstable selection of correlated predictors<br>
        <b>Tune:</b> λ (penalty strength)
      </div>
    </div>

  </div>

  <div class="rv-note">
    Regularization introduces shrinkage bias in exchange
    for potentially lower variance.
  </div>

</div>
```


## Identify Candidate Models: Regression

```{=html}
<div class="rv" style="--a:#478B77;--f:#E3F0E8">

  <div class="rv-nav">
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#557B9E;--f:#E3EDF5">1. Objective</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#557B9E;--f:#E3EDF5">2. Data</div>
    <div class="rv-tab on" style="--a:#478B77;--f:#E3F0E8">3. Candidate models</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#B28A45;--f:#F8EFD9">4. Training &amp; tuning</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#9876AC;--f:#EEE5F4">5. Selection</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#B8735D;--f:#F5E4DD">6. Evaluation</div>
  </div>

  <div class="rv-grid" style="--cols:3">

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>Regression splines</strong>
      <div>
        <b>Consider:</b> Smooth nonlinear relationships<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Smooth fit with local flexibility<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Choice of knots;
        potentially unstable behaviour near boundaries<br>
        <b>Tune:</b> Number and location of knots, degree<br><br>
        <b>Natural cubic splines:</b> Impose linearity beyond
        the boundary knots to reduce boundary instability.
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>k-NN regression</strong>
      <div>
        <b>Consider:</b> Nearby observations have similar
        responses; low-dimensional data<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> No specified
        functional form; simple to implement<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Sensitive to
        feature scales; curse of dimensionality<br>
        <b>Tune:</b> k (number of neighbours)
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>Local linear regression</strong>
      <div>
        <b>Consider:</b> Smooth nonlinear relationships
        with varying local trends<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Flexible fit;
        reduces boundary bias compared with local constant regression<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Curse of
        dimensionality; computational cost<br>
        <b>Tune:</b> Bandwidth
      </div>
    </div>

  </div>

  <div class="rv-note">
    Splines introduce flexibility through basis expansions,
    while k-NN and local linear regression make predictions
    using neighbouring observations.
  </div>

</div>
```


## Identify Candidate Models: Regression

```{=html}
<div class="rv" style="--a:#478B77;--f:#E3F0E8">

  <div class="rv-nav">
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#557B9E;--f:#E3EDF5">1. Objective</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#557B9E;--f:#E3EDF5">2. Data</div>
    <div class="rv-tab on" style="--a:#478B77;--f:#E3F0E8">3. Candidate models</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#B28A45;--f:#F8EFD9">4. Training &amp; tuning</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#9876AC;--f:#EEE5F4">5. Selection</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#B8735D;--f:#F5E4DD">6. Evaluation</div>
  </div>

  <div class="rv-grid" style="--cols:2">

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>Pruned regression tree</strong>
      <div>
        <b>Consider:</b> Nonlinear relationships;
        interpretability is important<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Automatically captures
        interactions; easy to visualize when small<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Potentially high variance;
        observations in the same terminal node receive
        the same prediction<br>
        <b>Tune:</b> Pruning parameter, tree depth
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>Bagging / Random forest</strong>
      <div>
        <b>Consider:</b> Nonlinear relationships; predictive performance is important<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Averages multiple trees
        to reduce variance; RF further reduces correlation
        between trees<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Less interpretable
        than a single tree; limited extrapolation<br>
        <b>Tune:</b> Number of trees, number of candidate
        predictors per split (RF)
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>Boosting</strong>
      <div>
        <b>Consider:</b> Nonlinear relationships;
        predictive performance is important<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Sequentially fits trees
        to correct previous prediction errors<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Less interpretable;
        can overfit if not appropriately tuned<br>
        <b>Tune:</b> Number of trees, learning rate, tree depth
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>Neural network</strong>
      <div>
        <b>Consider:</b> Complex nonlinear relationships; predictive performance is important; large sample size<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Highly flexible;
        learns complex relationships<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Less interpretable;
        computationally expensive; nonconvex optimization<br>
        <b>Tune:</b> Architecture, learning rate, regularization
      </div>
    </div>

  </div>

</div>
```

```{=html}
      <div>Models class-conditional distributions and

    </div>

      <strong>k-NN</strong>
      <div>Classifies observations based on
      neighbouring observations.</div>
    </div>

      <div>Constructs a large-margin decision boundary.</div>
    </div>

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>Trees / ensembles</strong>
      <div>Partitions the feature space into regions.</div>
    </div>

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>Neural networks</strong>
      <div>Learns complex nonlinear relationships between
      predictors and class probabilities.</div>
    </div>

  </div>

</div>
```


## Identify Candidate Models: Classification

```{=html}
<div class="rv" style="--a:#478B77;--f:#E3F0E8">

  <div class="rv-nav">
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#557B9E;--f:#E3EDF5">1. Objective</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#557B9E;--f:#E3EDF5">2. Data</div>
    <div class="rv-tab on" style="--a:#478B77;--f:#E3F0E8">3. Candidate models</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#B28A45;--f:#F8EFD9">4. Training &amp; tuning</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#9876AC;--f:#EEE5F4">5. Selection</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#B8735D;--f:#F5E4DD">6. Evaluation</div>
  </div>

  <div class="rv-grid" style="--cols:2">

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>Logistic regression (binary / multiclass)</strong>
      <div>
        <b>Consider:</b> Approximately linear log-odds; interpretation of predictor effects is important<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Interpretable coefficients;
        no class-conditional distribution assumptions<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Linear decision
        boundaries; no finite MLE under complete separation<br>
        <b>Tune:</b> None in basic model
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>LDA</strong>
      <div>
        <b>Consider:</b> Approximately Gaussian class-conditional
        distributions; common covariance<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Fewer parameters than QDA;
        pooled covariance estimate<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Linear decision
        boundaries; common covariance assumption<br>
        <b>Tune:</b> None in basic model
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>QDA</strong>
      <div>
        <b>Consider:</b> Approximately Gaussian class-conditional
        distributions; unequal covariances<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Allows quadratic
        decision boundaries<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> More parameters;
        Must estimate a separate covariance matrix for each class; estimates may be unstable
when sample sizes within classes are small<br>
        <b>Tune:</b> None in basic model
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>Naive Bayes</strong>
      <div>
        <b>Consider:</b> Conditional independence of
        predictors given class is plausible; many predictors relative to the sample size<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Simplifies estimation (fewer parameters than QDA);
        useful in high dimensions<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Conditional
        independence assumption may be unrealistic<br>
        <b>Tune:</b> None in basic model
      </div>
    </div>

  </div>

</div>
```

```{=html}
    <div class="rv-tab on" style="--a:#478B77;--f:#E3F0E8">3. Candidate models</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#B28A45;--f:#F8EFD9">4. Training &amp; tuning</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#9876AC;--f:#EEE5F4">5. Selection</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#B8735D;--f:#F5E4DD">6. Evaluation</div>
  </div>

  <div class="rv-grid" style="--cols:3">

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>k-NN</strong>
      <div>
        <b>Consider:</b> Nearby observations tend to belong
        to the same class; low-dimensional data<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> No specified functional
        form; flexible decision boundaries<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Sensitive to feature
        scales; curse of dimensionality<br>
        <b>Tune:</b> k (number of neighbours)
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>Linear SVM</strong>
      <div>
        <b>Consider:</b> Approximately linear decision boundary;
        class prediction is the primary objective<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Maximizes the margin;
        can handle overlapping classes using a soft margin<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Linear decision
        boundary; no direct posterior probability estimates<br>
        <b>Tune:</b> C (soft-margin cost parameter)
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>Kernel SVM</strong>
      <div>
        <b>Consider:</b> Nonlinear decision boundary;
        class prediction is the primary objective<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Captures complex
        nonlinear decision boundaries<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Sensitive to feature
        scales and tuning; less interpretable<br>
        <b>Tune:</b> C, kernel choice and kernel parameters
      </div>
    </div>

  </div>

  <div class="rv-note">
    Consider these methods when classification performance
    is more important than interpreting individual predictor
    effects, or when we wish to avoid specifying probability
    models. k-NN and nonlinear kernel SVMs also allow for more
    flexible decision boundaries.
  </div>

</div>
```


## Identify Candidate Models: Classification

```{=html}
<div class="rv" style="--a:#478B77;--f:#E3F0E8">

  <div class="rv-nav">
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#557B9E;--f:#E3EDF5">1. Objective</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#557B9E;--f:#E3EDF5">2. Data</div>
    <div class="rv-tab on" style="--a:#478B77;--f:#E3F0E8">3. Candidate models</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#B28A45;--f:#F8EFD9">4. Training &amp; tuning</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#9876AC;--f:#EEE5F4">5. Selection</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#B8735D;--f:#F5E4DD">6. Evaluation</div>
  </div>

  <div class="rv-grid" style="--cols:2">

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>Pruned classification tree</strong>
      <div>
        <b>Consider:</b> Nonlinear decision boundaries;
        interpretability is important<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Automatically captures
        interactions; easy to visualize when small<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Potentially high variance;
        observations in the same terminal node receive
        the same class prediction<br>
        <b>Tune:</b> Pruning parameter, tree depth
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>Bagging / Random forest</strong>
      <div>
        <b>Consider:</b> Nonlinear decision boundaries;
        predictive performance is more important
        than interpretability<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Reduces variance by
        combining trees; RF further reduces correlation
        between trees<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Less interpretable
        than a single tree; can still overfit<br>
        <b>Tune:</b> Number of trees, number of candidate
        predictors per split (RF)
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>Boosting</strong>
      <div>
        <b>Consider:</b> Nonlinear decision boundaries;
        predictive performance is more important
        than interpretability<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Combines simple trees
        sequentially to improve the fit; can reduce bias<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Less interpretable;
        sensitive to tuning; may overfit with too many iterations<br>
        <b>Tune:</b> Number of trees, learning rate, tree depth
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>Neural network</strong>
      <div>
        <b>Consider:</b> Complex nonlinear decision boundaries
        and interactions; sufficient training data<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Learns complex nonlinear
        relationships between predictors and class probabilities<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Less interpretable;
        computationally expensive; nonconvex optimization<br>
        <b>Tune:</b> Architecture, learning rate, regularization
      </div>
    </div>

  </div>

  <div class="rv-note">
    These methods can automatically capture nonlinear decision
    boundaries and interactions without specifying them in
    advance, often at the expense of interpretability.
  </div>

</div>
```

Data</div><div class="rv-tab on" style="--a:#478B77;--f:#E3F0E8">3. Candidate models</div><div class="rv-tab " style="--a:#B28A45;--f:#F8EFD9">4. Training &amp; tuning</div><div class="rv-tab " style="--a:#9876AC;--f:#EEE5F4">5. Selection</div><div class="rv-tab " style="--a:#B8735D;--f:#F5E4DD">6. Evaluation</div></div><div class="rv-grid" style="--cols:2"><div class="rv-card"><strong>PCA</strong><div><b>Consider:</b> Reduce dimension / visualize<br><b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Retains maximal variance for linear projections<br><b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Scaling; variance need not imply predictive relevance<br><b>Tune:</b> Number of PCs</div></div><div class="rv-card"><strong>K-means</strong><div><b>Consider:</b> Find compact groups<br><b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Simple cluster summaries<br><b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Scaling, initialization, outliers<br><b>Tune:</b> Number of clusters K</div></div></div><div class="rv-note">PCA can precede K-means or supervised models.</div></div>

## Model Selection: Feature Selection

```{=html}
<div class="rv" style="--a:#9876AC;--f:#EEE5F4">

  <div class="rv-nav">
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#557B9E;--f:#E3EDF5">1. Objective</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#557B9E;--f:#E3EDF5">2. Data</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#478B77;--f:#E3F0E8">3. Candidate models</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#B28A45;--f:#F8EFD9">4. Training &amp; tuning</div>
    <div class="rv-tab on" style="--a:#9876AC;--f:#EEE5F4">5. Selection</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#B8735D;--f:#F5E4DD">6. Evaluation</div>
  </div>

  <div class="rv-root">Which predictors should we include?</div>

  <div class="rv-grid" style="--cols:2">

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>Best subset selection</strong>
      <div>
        Consider all possible subsets of predictors.<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Finds the best-fitting
        subset for each model size<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Computationally expensive
        as the number of predictors increases
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>Forward stepwise selection</strong>
      <div>
        Start with no predictors and add one at a time.<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Computationally cheaper
        than best subset selection<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Greedy search;
        may miss the optimal subset
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>Backward stepwise selection</strong>
      <div>
        Start with all predictors and remove one at a time.<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Computationally cheaper
        than best subset selection<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Greedy search;
        the full model must be estimable
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="rv-card">
      <strong>LASSO</strong>
      <div>
        Shrink some coefficients to exactly zero.<br>
        <b class="rv-plus">Advantage:</b> Simultaneous
        regularization and feature selection<br>
        <b class="rv-minus">Limitation:</b> Potentially unstable
        selection of correlated predictors
      </div>
    </div>

  </div>

</div>
```

## Model Selection: Comparing Candidate Models

```{=html}
<div class="rv" style="--a:#9876AC;--f:#EEE5F4">

  <div class="rv-nav">
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#557B9E;--f:#E3EDF5">1. Objective</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#557B9E;--f:#E3EDF5">2. Data</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#478B77;--f:#E3F0E8">3. Candidate models</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#B28A45;--f:#F8EFD9">4. Training &amp; tuning</div>
    <div class="rv-tab on" style="--a:#9876AC;--f:#EEE5F4">5. Selection</div>
    <div class="rv-tab" style="--a:#B8735D;--f:#F5E4DD">6. Evaluation</div>
  </div>

  <div class="rv-root">How do we compare candidate models?</div>

  <div class="rv-branches" style="--cols:3">

    <div class="rv-branch">
      <div class="rv-head">Linear regression criteria</div>

      <div class="rv-card">
        <strong>Adjusted R² ↑</strong>
        <div>Adjusts goodness of fit for the number
        of predictors.</div>
      </div>

      <div class="rv-card">
        <strong>Mallows' Cp ↓</strong>
        <div>Accounts for model complexity when
        estimating prediction error.</div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="rv-branch">
      <div class="rv-head">Likelihood-based criteria</div>

      <div class="rv-card">
        <strong>AIC ↓</strong>
        <div>Balances likelihood and model complexity.</div>
      </div>

      <div class="rv-card">
        <strong>BIC ↓</strong>
        <div>Typically penalizes model complexity more
        strongly than AIC.</div>
      </div>
    </div>

    <div class="rv-branch">
      <div class="rv-head">Validation methods</div>

      <div class="rv-card">
        <strong>Validation set approach</strong>
        <div>Estimate prediction error using a separate
        validation set.</div>
      </div>

      <div class="rv-card">
        <strong>Cross-validation</strong>
        <div>Estimate out-of-sample prediction error
        across multiple training and validation splits.</div>
      </div>
    </div>

  </div>

</div>
```

## Activity 1: Predicting House Prices

A real estate company has collected data on 2,000 houses, including 30 predictors such as square footage, age, location, number of bedrooms and lot size. Some predictors are highly correlated, and exploratory analysis suggests that some relationships with house price are nonlinear.

<br> 

The company wants to accurately predict the selling price of new listings but would also like to understand which features contribute to higher house prices.

<br> 

:::{.fragment} 
Discuss your thoughts on the following questions with the people around you: 

- Which three models would you consider fitting? Why? 
- How would you compare the candidate models?  
:::


## Activity 2: Classifying Patients

Researchers collect data on 400 patients, including 15 measurements, to predict whether a patient has a particular medical condition. Approximately 10% of patients have the condition.

<br> 

Some predictors appear approximately normally distributed within each class, but the researchers are unsure whether the covariance matrices are equal. They also suspect that some relationships may be nonlinear. 

<br> 

:::{.fragment} 
Discuss your thoughts on the following questions with the people around you: 

- Which classifiers would you consider? Why? 
- Are there any models that you would be hesitant to fit? 
- How would you compare predictive performance? 
:::

## Activity 3: Flexibility 

A researcher fits four regression models to the same dataset. All relevant hyperparameters have been selected using five-fold cross-validation.

| Model          | Training MSE | CV MSE |
|:---------------|:------------:|:------:|
| OLS            | 24.5         | 26.8   |
| Ridge          | 25.2         | 25.9   |
| Random forest  | 8.4          | 25.5   |
| Neural network | 3.1          | 25.4   |

<br> 

:::{.fragment} 
Discuss your thoughts on the following questions with the people around you: 

- Which model here is the most flexible? Least flexible? 
- Which model would you select? Why?
- What can we learn from the differences between the training and cross validation errors? 
:::


## Activity 4: Discovering Structure in Customer Data 

A company collects 50 measurements on 5,000 customers, describing their purchasing habits. Many of the measurements are highly correlated and are measured on different scales.

<br> 

The company suspects that there are different types of customers but does not know how many groups exist.

<br> 

:::{.fragment} 
Discuss your thoughts on the following questions with the people around you: 

- Would you apply PCA, K-Means clustering, or both? Why? 
- How would you select the number of principal components/clusters?
- How would you determine whether the clusters are meaningful? 
:::

## Final Thoughts

Machine learning is not about memorizing a collection of algorithms or finding the most sophisticated model.

It is about learning to:

- Ask meaningful questions.
- Understand the data in front of you.
- Recognize the assumptions and limitations of your methods.
- Make informed decisions and justify your choices.

<br>

:::{.fragment}
::: {style="text-align:center; color:#478B77; font-size:1.1em;"}
**"All models are wrong, but some are useful." - George Box**
:::

<br>

If there is one thing you take away from this course, I hope it is not just *how* to fit a model, but *why* you would choose to fit it in the first place.
:::
